theme.appSubtitle: Energy‑aware planning for women navigating menopause.

cycle._note_for_devs: No menstrual phases. Instead, an energy/symptom model drives all recommendations. The user logs their energy state daily, plus optional symptoms (hot flashes, sleep quality, joint pain, mood). The app does NOT track cycle days or predict a period.
cycle._persona: Demo persona: woman in her late 50s, post-menopause, based in Pune, India. Vegetarian diet with iron intake as an ongoing concern (common with a no-meat diet + heavier periods earlier in life). Physical activity baseline is modest — walking, light housework — not a gym habit, so guidance should build up gently rather than assume athletic fitness. Her primary creative/intellectual practice is singing (riyaz/bhajans), not deep-work or study.

high.label: High Energy
high.desc: Clear head, good stamina. Your body is ready for a bit more today — a longer walk, a full riyaz session, time with people. Use it.
needs: A longer walk than usual, or a full singing/riyaz session
Iron-rich meal — dal, palak, or ragi today
Social time if you have the energy for it

moderate.label: Moderate Energy
moderate.desc: Steady state. A daily walk, a bit of singing, home-cooked meals on time. This is your sustainable baseline — it's good, and it's enough.
needs: Balanced meals with dal, vegetables, and good fats

low.label: Rest & Restore
low.desc: Rest is the workout today. Gentle movement, extra water, and permission to go slow. This is hormonal — it will pass.
needs: Gentle yoga or a short walk only
Extra sleep and no guilt about it

energyModel.checkInPrompt: How does your body feel today?

hormoneModel.note: The natural hormone cycle curve is not shown because the menstrual phase model does not apply. Planning is based on your energy check-in and symptom log instead.

low.note: Skip the walk today if you need to. A little stretching at home is enough. Honor the low-energy day.

moderate.note: A comfortable walk or some time in the garden — steady is the goal, not intense.

high.note: Your best-energy day. A longer walk than usual, or try adding a few minutes of gentle strength work.

low.note: A few familiar bhajans, nothing that takes effort to learn. Let it be comforting, not a practice session.

moderate.note: Good day for regular riyaz — work on breath control or a piece you're refining.

high.note: Your clearest, most energetic day — a good window to learn a new raag or piece.

morningWalk.label: 🌅 Morning Walk
morningWalk.note: Cooler Pune mornings are the easiest window before the day heats up.

warmBath.label: ♨️ Warm Bath
warmBath.note: Heat therapy can ease joint pain and improve sleep onset — especially valuable post-menopause.

Light strength — resistance band or bodyweight

PM.name: Full riyaz session — work on a new piece

AM.name: Gentle seated stretching — no effort needed
Short walk — even 10–15 min is enough

cycleFocusOptions.label: 🩸 Iron & Energy
cycleFocusOptions.note: Vegetarian diets need extra attention to iron. Dal, palak, ragi, and jaggery at every meal where possible. Pair with vitamin C, skip tea/coffee right after eating.

cycleFocusOptions.label: 🧘 Mobility & Joint Health
cycleFocusOptions.note: Gentle yoga-forward. Shorter walks, more stretching. Warm baths built into most evenings.

cycleFocusOptions.label: 🦴 Bone Strength
cycleFocusOptions.note: Even light resistance work (bands, bodyweight) 2x/week protects bone density. Calcium-rich vegetarian foods matter — dairy, til, ragi.

cycleFocusOptions.label: ✨ Balanced Weekly Rhythm
cycleFocusOptions.note: A walk most days, riyaz whenever the mood strikes, rest when the body asks. No rigid plan.

activity._note: This archetype's baseline physical activity is modest by design — gentle, achievable movement matters more than intensity. Iron and calcium intake (common concerns on a vegetarian diet) are prioritized alongside bone density.

food.intro: Vegetarian diets need real attention to iron, B12, and calcium — especially post-menopause when bone density drops faster. None of this needs to be complicated: dal, palak, ragi, and jaggery, eaten consistently, go a long way.

high.headline: Iron-forward, energising
eat: Dal or rajma at both lunch and dinner — protein + iron
Palak or other leafy greens, cooked with a squeeze of lemon (vitamin C helps iron absorption)
Ragi roti or ragi porridge — calcium and iron
Jaggery instead of refined sugar where possible
Til (sesame) or peanut chikki as a snack — calcium and healthy fats
limit: Tea or coffee right after meals (tannins block iron absorption — wait an hour)
high.note: Good-energy days are the days to be consistent with dal and greens — the iron adds up over the week, not from any single meal.

moderate.headline: Steady, calcium-rich, gut-friendly
eat: Curd or buttermilk at lunch — calcium and probiotics
Sabzi with a little ghee — helps absorb fat-soluble vitamins
Sprouted moong or chana — easy protein
Seasonal fruit — guava, papaya, or amla for vitamin C
moderate.note: Bone density loss is silent until it isn't. A cup of curd, some dal, and a handful of til across the day is more useful than any single 'superfood.'

low.headline: Warm, easy to digest
eat: Khichdi — gentle on digestion, still gives protein from dal + rice
Moong dal soup or clear vegetable soup
Warm haldi doodh (turmeric milk) before bed
Banana or dates for a gentle energy lift
Ginger tea for digestion — not caffeinated chai
limit: Spicy or oily food (harder to digest on a low day)
low.note: Low days are for khichdi and haldi doodh, not willpower. Let the food be gentle — the body is already asking for rest.

fasting._note: Menopausal women should be more cautious with extended fasting. Muscle loss risk increases without adequate protein. Recommend max 16:8 and only on moderate/high energy days.

high.reason: High energy days tolerate fasting better. Keep protein high when you break the fast.

moderate.reason: A 14-hour overnight fast supports insulin sensitivity without stressing cortisol.

low.reason: On low-energy days, fasting can worsen fatigue and cortisol. Prioritize nourishment.

milestones.label: Glycogen depleting
milestones.bio: Your body is burning through stored glucose. Hunger is normal — it's just your ghrelin pattern.

milestones.label: Ketone shift begins
milestones.bio: Insulin is dropping. Your body is starting to shift toward fat oxidation.

milestones.label: Overnight reset
milestones.bio: A gentle overnight fast is complete. This is a great stopping point for menopausal women.

milestones.label: Ideal window
milestones.bio: 14 hours is a sweet spot — metabolic benefits without muscle-loss risk.

milestones.label: Extended — be mindful
milestones.bio: Extended fasting on top of hormonal changes can stress cortisol. Break with protein first.

sexualHealth.note: Post-menopause (12+ months since last period) — fertility is no longer a consideration.
sexualHealth.disclaimer: This app is a planning tool, not medical advice. Always consult your provider for health decisions.

medications.disclaimer: Iron and B12 deficiency are common on a vegetarian diet and can mimic or worsen menopause fatigue — worth checking with a doctor rather than assuming it's 'just hormones.' Always follow your provider's advice.

ui.safetyDisclaimer: This is a planning dashboard, not a diagnostic tool. Nothing here is medical advice. Discuss all health decisions with your provider.
